question: If cot²θ=(1)/((1-a²)), |a| < 1, and θ is an acute angle, then find the value of (sec θ + cosec θ tan³ θ).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Expression = sec θ + (1 / sin θ) × (sin³ θ / cos³ θ) = sec θ + (sin² θ / cos³ θ)

⇒ Expression = sec θ + (1 / cos θ) × (sin² θ / cos² θ) = sec θ + sec θ × tan² θ

⇒ Expression = sec θ × (1 + tan² θ) = sec θ × sec² θ = sec³ θ

⇒ Given cot² θ = 1 ÷ (1 − a²) → tan² θ = 1 − a²

⇒ sec² θ = 1 + tan² θ = 1 + 1 − a² = 2 − a²

⇒ Final Value = sec³ θ = (sec² θ)³/² = (2 − a²)³/²

**∴ The correct answer is (2 − a²)³/².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ cot² θ = 1 ÷ (1 − a²)

⇒ cot θ = 1 ÷ √(1 − a²) = Base ÷ Perpendicular

**Calculations:**

⇒ By Pythagoras Theorem, Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

⇒ AC² = BC² + AB² = 1² + [√(1 − a²)]²

⇒ AC² = 1 + 1 − a² = 2 − a²

⇒ Hypotenuse (AC) = √(2 − a²)

⇒ sec θ = Hypotenuse ÷ Base = √(2 − a²) ÷ 1 = √(2 − a²)

⇒ tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base = √(1 − a²) ÷ 1 = √(1 − a²)

⇒ cosec θ = Hypotenuse ÷ Perpendicular = √(2 − a²) ÷ √(1 − a²)

⇒ Given expression = sec θ + cosec θ × tan³ θ

⇒ Expression = √(2 − a²) + [√(2 − a²) ÷ √(1 − a²)] × [√(1 − a²)]³

⇒ Expression = √(2 − a²) + √(2 − a²) × [√(1 − a²)]²

⇒ Expression = √(2 − a²) + √(2 − a²) × (1 − a²)

⇒ Expression = √(2 − a²) × [1 + (1 − a²)] = √(2 − a²) × (2 − a²)

⇒ Expression = (2 − a²)¹/² × (2 − a²)¹ = (2 − a²)³/²

**∴ The correct answer is (2 − a²)³/².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Trigonometric Identities

The three primary identities are: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, sec² θ − tan² θ = 1, and cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1.

Reciprocal Relations

Functions are inverses of each other: sin θ = 1/cosec θ, cos θ = 1/sec θ, and tan θ = 1/cot θ.

Geometric Interpretation

In a right-angled triangle, the trigonometric ratios are defined as relationships between sides. For example, sec θ is the ratio of the hypotenuse to the adjacent base, while cosec θ represents the ratio of the hypotenuse to the perpendicular side.
